name: Build orchestrator
author: Brett
description: Breaks every build into small steps (30 min or less), each pinned to Fable or Opus, and runs the build pipeline (Brett, Nov 8 2026): every build gets an id and a Claude split (Fable only where needed) and sits in Pending; Brett moves it to the Queue; the dispatcher (pipeline.mjs on the VPS, every minute) watches the Claude accounts (which have Fable, parallel per account) and the agent slots and, when a slot is free, starts a headless session for the next Queue build on an account that runs its next phase's model. The only place that browses and manages builds (Brett, Nov 10 2026; the Build manager is retired): tabs Pending, Queue (each build's steps, planned model and account), Active, Incomplete, Complete, Errors, then Accounts (health every 5 minutes: sign-in, credits, Fable), All builds, Approvals and Rules. When a build's turn comes the dispatcher makes the final account pick, subscriptions first (in Brett's order), then any API account, moving on until one accepts, and records which account took it. Tracker is the one builds store, _claude/builds/store.json, so any session or account continues the build (orchestrator.mjs next | brief | act; pipeline.mjs status | queue | unqueue | split | tick).

items.title: Build priorities
items.description: Every build's priority tag (Urgent, High, Normal, Low = P0-P3) and how many things wait on it.

items.title: What's waiting on a build
items.description: A build's priority and everything waiting for it: builds behind it in the agent queue, builds that depend on it, PRs stacked on it or behind it in the merge queue, UI Review items, linked plans. Say 'what's waiting on skins'.
items.output: { id, title, priority, label, waiting: [{ kind, id, title, why }] }

items.title: Headless runs and start tokens
items.description: A build's headless runs: start tokens (the context of the first request), cost, brief only or full chain, tools and MCP servers loaded. Say 'what did skins start with'.
items.output: { build, runs: [{ session, briefOnly, startTokens, startCostUsd, costUsd, at }] }

items.title: Set build priority
items.description: Set the priority of one or more builds: 'make banner widgets urgent'. Higher priority starts first in the agent queue and lands first in the merge queue; Brett's manual moves still win.

priority.description: urgent, high, normal, low or P0-P3

items.title: What Brett said
items.description: The verbatim words Brett used to start a build (build-origin@1): when, where, who launched it, the brief and later addenda.

items.title: Record what Brett said
items.description: Record Brett's verbatim words on a build that has none (backfilled ones give way); his words are never replaced: use origin-addendum for a later change.

said.description: Brett's exact words, verbatim and unedited (never a paraphrase)

items.title: Add what Brett said later
items.description: Append a later change Brett asked for (verbatim) to a build's origin.

said.description: Brett's exact words, verbatim and unedited (never a paraphrase)

items.title: Pipeline status
items.description: The build pipeline: what is Pending, in the Queue and Building, every Claude account (Fable yes or no, how many run on it), the agent slots, and what the dispatcher's next tick will start or why it waits. Say 'what's in the queue' or 'is anything building'.
items.output: { table: { pending, queued, building }, accounts, accountsFrom: { source, at, ageMin, why }, slots, plan: { launches, waits, idle }, state: { selfCheck, selfCheckRequested, … } }

items.title: Dispatcher self-check
items.description: Ask the dispatcher to check every Claude account one by one (signed in, limited, API key saved and not rejected, free slots), release slots and builds held by sessions that ended, and rebuild its account list. Runs on the VPS on the next tick (within a minute); the result shows on the Pipeline tab and in pipeline status (state.selfCheck), and AmberX hears when it fixed something or found an account it can't use. Say 'check the build accounts' or 'why is nothing building'.

reason.description: Why the check was asked for

items.output: { ran: false, requested, last: { at, line, fixes, problems, findings } }

items.title: Orchestrator tab
items.description: One of the orchestrator's tabs: pending, queue, active, incomplete, complete or errors, with each build's steps, planned model and account, and the account that took it. Say 'what's in the queue' or 'show build errors'.
items.output: { tab, rows: [{ id, title, status, steps, stepList, pipeline: { planned, account, pickedAt, tried } }] }

items.title: Claude account health
items.description: The last account health sweep (every 5 minutes, headless, never touches a build): per account, can sign in, has credits, accepts Fable. Say 'are the accounts healthy'.
items.output: { health: { at, line, problems, accounts: [{ name, kind, signedIn, credits, fable, error }] }, every }

items.title: Check the Claude accounts now
items.description: Run the account health sweep now (the dispatcher starts it within a minute, in the background). Say 'check the accounts now'.

items.title: Queue a build
items.description: Move a Pending build to the Queue: the dispatcher starts it when a slot and an account for its model are free. Say 'queue the icon browser build'. Right before it moves, the orchestrator checks it against main: already done or superseded = closed and archived instead, partly done = only what is left is queued.

items.title: Main checks
items.description: Every recorded check of a build against main (at queue and at dispatch): verdict, why, steps ticked, PR / commit.
items.output: { checks: { <build>: { verdict, why, ticks, stage, at } } }

items.title: Check a build against main
items.description: Check one build against main now: Shipped features, its PR, its branch and the files its steps name. Dry unless apply: already done or superseded = closed and archived (AmberX told), partly done = the steps already on main are ticked. The orchestrator does this by itself before it queues a build and again at dispatch. Say 'is the icon browser build already on main'.

apply.description: Act on the verdict (default: only report it)

items.output: { id, verdict: done|partial|superseded|open|unknown, why, ticks, pr, commit, applied }

items.title: Take a build out of the Queue
items.description: Move a queued build back to Pending before it starts.

items.title: Split a build into steps
items.description: Ask the orchestrator to split (or re-split) a build into steps of 30 minutes or less, Fable only where needed; done by the dispatcher within a minute.

items.title: Ask for a build
items.description: File a build with the orchestrator and put it in the Queue: the orchestrator is the only thing that starts builds; it assigns the id, splits it and the dispatcher launches it on the right account and model. Say 'build me …'.

queue.description: Straight to the Queue (default true); false = Pending

items.title: Route a build to API or subscriptions
items.description: Where one build may run: api (API-key accounts only, billed per token under their daily and weekly caps; Brett's own click), subscription (never an API account) or auto (subscriptions, API only by the overflow rule).

items.title: Pipeline settings
items.description: The dispatcher's settings, including the API overflow rule (apiOverflow) and which API accounts it may use.

items.title: Change pipeline settings
items.description: Change dispatcher settings. apiOverflow = when every subscription account is full or out, send builds to an API-key account (off by default; turning it on is Brett's own click, anyone may turn it off).

mainCheck.description: The check against main before queueing: code = plain evidence, ai = also ask Claude when code finds nothing, off = never
